title: Expansion and cytotoxicity of mucosal CAR + T cells in enterocolitis associated with BCMA CAR-T cell therapy
desc: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) is a B cell maturation-antigen-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell product approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treatment. Previously reported cases of post-cilta-cel immune effector cell enterocolitis (IEC-EC) have been described as a severe diarrhea associated with clonal CAR T cell populations. Here we report nine cases of cilta-cel-associated IEC-EC with CAR T cell-positive (CAR+) infiltration in 158 cilta-cel-treated patients at MD Anderson Cancer Center (incidence of 5.1% at a 6-month landmark and 5.7% globally). Cilta-cel infiltration was the primary cause of IEC-EC, and all cases demonstrated monoclonal or oligoclonal T cell populations as measured by vector integration analysis, flow cytometry and T cell receptor sequencing. Patients with IEC-EC had 100-fold more CAR T cell persistence in the peripheral blood than patients without IEC-EC. RNA sequencing analysis revealed increased cytotoxic and inflammatory programs associated with the CAR+ infiltrates relative to controls. Clonal vector integration occurred in introns of highly expressed genes without evidence of vector-mediated mutagenesis. Candidate driver mutations were sparse and heterogeneous, distinguishing IEC-EC from peripheral T cell lymphoma following CAR T cell therapy. In sum, we find that IEC-EC pathology represents a distinct, duodenum-predominant, clonal lymphoproliferative disorder characterized by the infiltration of clonal CAR+ cytotoxic T cells into the gastrointestinal tract.

title: ECG foundation models for cardiovascular screening in a cohort of young competitive athletes
desc: AI-powered cardiac screening could evolve sports medicine by boosting accuracy, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, with automated ECG interpretation based on foundation models becoming key for large-scale athlete screening. Before deployment, it is crucial to verify whether these clinically developed models are applicable to this population. We evaluated whether ECG foundation models trained on general clinical populations can diagnose athlete-specific ECG findings. We fine-tuned three models (ECG-FM, HuBERT-ECG, ECGFounder) on PhysioNet/CinC 2021, 87,662 samples, and tested them on 43 expert-annotated ECGs from highly trained/national-level athletes. Performance was strong on PhysioNet/CinC 2021 (AUROC 0.97, AUPRC 0.57, Sensitivity 0.89) but dropped on athletes’ data, confirming domain shift. ECGFounder performed best (AUROC 0.84, AUPRC 0.72, Sensitivity 0.57) and detected the most frequent findings, Sinus Bradycardia (AUROC 0.87) and Sinus Arrhythmia (AUROC 0.95), well. Per-label estimates for rare classes must be interpreted cautiously, given the small cohort. This work contributes to developing athlete-focused AI frameworks for reliable ECG-based screening.

title: Artificial intelligence and triple negative breast cancer: can pathomics help oncologists?
desc: [Frontiers in oncology] Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive and heterogeneous subtype of breast cancer with limited targeted therapies and poor prognosis. Recent advances in digital pathology and artificial intelligence (AI) are transforming traditional, qualitative histopathology into quantitative, data-driven analysis. Within computational pathology, pathomics (the extraction of handcrafted, high-dimensional features from digitized histological images) and deep learning (DL)-based whole-slide image analysis have been investigated for the prediction of molecular subtypes, biomarker expression, tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes, and treatment response in TNBC. AI models, including DL and multimodal systems integrating histopathology, omics, and clinical data, are being explored for patient stratification, risk assessment, and therapy personalization, encompassing chemotherapy, immunotherapy, PARP inhibitors, and antibody-drug conjugates. By linking spatial tissue architecture with molecular profiles, these approaches may provide new insights into tumor biology and the tumor microenvironment. Most TNBC-specific studies are retrospective, small or single-center, few have been externally validated and, to our knowledge, none has yet demonstrated clinical utility in prospective trials; prediction of biomarkers such as PD-L1 or homologous recombination deficiency from hematoxylin and eosin slides remains investigational and cannot replace validated testing. Despite these challenges, AI-assisted computational pathology is a promising decision-support tool, which complements and does not replace pathologists and oncologists, for enhancing diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic decision-making in TNBC.

title: Pragmatic AI-Assisted Lung Cancer Translational Study
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Sir Run Run Shaw Hospital; conditions: Lung Cancer, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Large Language Model; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 150; status: RECRUITING] The goal of this study is to learn whether an artificial intelligence (AI) tool helps healthcare providers write and revise medical notes and check medical orders. This prospective study compares routine documentation without AI to documentation with AI assistance. The AI tool helps draft notes and review orders, but it does not make treatment decisions. Researchers will compare the quality of the notes, the time spent writing them, and the number of order errors between the two methods. The results will help hospitals decide if AI can improve daily clinical workflows.

title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
desc: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Deep Learning for Prediction of Radiation-Induced Xerostomia in Head and Neck Cancer
desc: To develop and evaluate an uncertainty-aware multimodal learning framework for predicting radiation-induced xerostomia in patients receiving head-and-neck cancer radiotherapy. We developed a Bidirectional Attention-enhanced Diffusion Transformer (BA-DiT) that combines self-supervised multimodal representation learning with supervised Bayesian fine-tuning. The model integrates pretreatment CT images and three-dimensional dose distributions, focusing on bilateral parotid glands while incorporating surrounding anatomical and dosimetric information. During pretraining, bidirectional cross-attention integrates anatomical and dosimetric features, while a latent Diffusion Transformer learns joint representations through diffusion-based learning, feature reconstruction, and contrastive alignment. Supervised fine-tuning employs a Bayesian classifier to predict individualized xerostomia risk and quantify predictive uncertainty, with a learnable label-transition model accounting for potential toxicity label uncertainty. BA-DiT was developed using four independent cohorts (Moffitt, Emory, MSHS, and TCIA) and evaluated against baseline and ablation models. Evaluation included predictive performance, calibration, uncertainty quantification, decision curve analysis, and patient-level case studies. In independent MSHS and Emory cohorts, BA-DiT achieved AUCs of 0.83 and 0.80, respectively, outperforming baseline models. Predictive uncertainty peaked near the decision boundary, with aleatoric uncertainty being the predominant component. Uncertainty-based selective prediction generally improved net benefit among retained patients, with greater gains at lower prediction coverage. BA-DiT enables individualized xerostomia risk prediction while providing complementary uncertainty estimates, potentially supporting informed clinical decision-making and personalized toxicity management.

title: Patient-Expressed Needs, Burdens and Barriers in Taiwanese Online Health Discussions: A Taiwan-Contextualized Friction Framework Applied With Large Language Model-Based Social Listening
desc: Background: Patients' difficulties with illness and care (not understanding a result, distress, daily restrictions, not knowing where to go, family strain) may not surface in clinical encounters or records. Regulatory guidance on patient-focused drug development recognizes social-media listening as a source of patient experience data, but no systematic framework exists for Traditional Chinese discussions in Taiwan, and keyword pipelines measure such content poorly. Objective: To characterize patient-expressed needs, burdens and barriers ("frictions") in Taiwanese online health discussions with an eight-domain, Taiwan-contextualized framework, identify whose frictions they are, and assess how securely each is measured. Methods: From a 13.6-million-unit archive of the PTT forum and three ask-a-physician services, seeded samples of 9,131 pipeline-flagged units and 1,000 unflagged forum articles (10,130 distinct units) were read in full by a large language model under rubrics for relevance, author (patient or family member) and eight domains: information gap, emotional burden, lifestyle burden, medication experience, system navigation, access barrier, caregiver burden and cost burden. Profiles were reported separately for forum articles and physician submissions and checked against a second vendor, two physicians' independent labels of 160 accepted and rejected units, and the archive's keyword pipeline. Results: Among 2,395 model-confirmed forum articles, 83.1% voiced at least one friction: information gap 59.5% (physicians 86%-93%), emotional burden 39.0%, medication experience 24.1%, lifestyle burden 22.2% and system navigation 16.3%; access barrier, caregiver burden and cost burden were each below 7%. Of 3,105 submissions, nearly all were questions and 53.8% also carried a burden. Navigation rarely concerned insurance (9.1%). Family-authored forum articles (14.5%) more often voiced emotional burden (54.9% vs 36.3%), navigation (34.8% vs 13.2%; instrument-dependent) and access barriers (16.4% vs 4.7%), and patient-authored articles lifestyle burden (24.8% vs 6.9%); caregiver burden came with emotional burden in 86.0% of articles voicing it. Emotional and lifestyle burden were commoner in forum articles than submissions under the model, a second vendor and both physicians; medication experience and navigation were instrument-dependent, and physicians disagreed on cost (32% vs 4%). title: NeuroSim: a clinically informed multi-disorder EEG simulator with personalized pattern injection and AI-driven neurological modeling
desc: Deep learning for electroencephalography (EEG) based neurodiagnostics is constrained by the limited availability of labeled clinical recordings. Datasets covering Alzheimers disease (AD), Parkinsons disease (PD), schizophrenia (SCZ), epilepsy (EPI), and frontotemporal dementia (FTD) are scarce, demographically narrow, and heterogeneous across acquisition sites, while privacy requirements restrict data sharing. Existing EEG simulators typically address a single disorder or trade biological interpretability for statistical fidelity. This study presents NeuroSim, a simulation framework that generates synthetic multichannel EEG with user-controlled injection of disease-specific patterns across five disorders and multiple severity levels. A physiologically motivated baseline generator produces band-limited rhythms, event-related potentials, artifacts, and hierarchical subject-level and trial-level variability. Disease patterns are introduced through region-specific and severity-specific spectral modulation that encodes established biomarkers, including posterior alpha suppression in AD, motor beta enhancement in PD, and spike-wave discharges in EPI. An interactive interface exposes montage, sampling rate, duration, artifacts, stimuli, affected regions, and severity, and exports signals with reproducible metadata. The simulated signals reproduced the expected biomarker directionality under spectral, topographic, and multivariate statistical analysis. A convolutional-attention classifier trained on simulated data reached 95.3 to 96.8 percent hold-out accuracy, and post hoc explainability analyses produced class-separable embeddings with attributions concentrated on pathophysiologically expected electrodes. Application of the analysis pipeline to recordings from the Temple University Hospital EEG Corpus confirmed compatibility with heterogeneous clinical data. In subject-level augmentation experiments on real clinical EEG, supplementing real training data with NeuroSim samples increased classification accuracy from 91.6 to 94.5 percent for AD versus healthy controls and from 90.9 to 94.0 percent for PD versus healthy controls, exceeding the improvement obtained with conventional signal-level augmentation. NeuroSim is released as open-source software to support augmentation, benchmarking, and explainable artificial intelligence in neurological diagnostics.

title: Virtual atrial fibrillation dynamics reflect clinical outcomes after catheter ablation
desc: Chamber-wide assessment of restitution dynamics is not feasible in vivo during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. We reconstructed left-atrial digital twins from high-density (HD) bipolar electroanatomical maps in 323 patients, computed node-level restitution steepness (maximal restitution slope [Smax]; >0.4 million nodes), and induced virtual AF with standardized ramp pacing to classify sustainability (sustained ≥16 s vs non-sustained <16 s), excluding 32 cases with extensive low-voltage substrate and depressed mean Smax. We found that clustering of HD restitution profiles identifies four restitution patterns that stratify clinical atrial arrhythmia recurrence, with the Overall-Low pattern (aHR, 0.37) and the Average-Homogeneous pattern (aHR, 0.59) each showing lower risk than the Overall-High pattern. Furthermore, non-sustained virtual AF independently predicted lower recurrence (aHR: 0.27). Adding restitution pattern and sustainability to clinical covariates improved discrimination (ΔHarrell’s C-index: 0.050), and the combined digital-twin model remained incremental after adjustment for low-voltage area burden, supporting digital-twin outputs as complementary functional descriptors for risk stratification after pulmonary vein isolation.

title: Multimodal digital biomarker for asthma: complementary roles of vocal, clinical and demographic factors
desc: Asthma affects over 260 million people worldwide, yet diagnosis remains dependent on spirometry and specialist assessment, limiting accessibility in primary care and low-resource settings. Vocal biomarkers offer a promising non-invasive alternative, but prior studies have largely focused on acoustic features without integrating clinical context. We present a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts framework for asthma identification that adaptively combines acoustic embeddings from sustained vowel phonation and reading passage tasks with structured clinical and demographic data. The model was evaluated on a matched cohort of 1218 self-reported asthma cases and healthy controls from the Colive Voice study. The multimodal model achieved an AUROC of 0.83 and Brier score of 0.18, outperforming unimodal approaches. Exploratory analysis of the gating mechanism in asthma cases showed that greater respiratory symptom burden was associated with increased weighting of reading-passage modality and reduced weighting of sustained-vowel phonation modality. These findings support the feasibility of voice-based identification of self-reported asthma; however, independent prospective validation remains necessary before clinical use.

title: AI-Driven Analysis of Patient-Derived Models.
source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] As a crucial component in preclinical cancer research, patient-derived models (PDMs) are experiencing a substantial transformation due to AI integration. AI improves the conversion efficiency of PDMs' static-dynamic predictions through cross-modal data integration and supports a comprehensive precision medicine technology platform that encompasses everything from molecular mechanisms to clinical translation. In clinical translation, the "AI-PDMs" system is revolutionizing oncology drug development and enabling personalized treatment decisions, moving from experience-based methods to data-driven strategies. This paper provides a detailed summary of AI's innovative uses of PDMs, such as machine learning-based high-dimensional pharmacological sensitivity data mining, deep learning-enhanced 3D tumor microenvironment modeling, and computer vision-driven advancements in pathological feature annotation, thereby offering a systematic framework for future cancer diagnosis and treatment innovations.

title: AI-Assisted vs. Traditional Simulation for Safe Surgery Checklist Knowledge and Skills
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Lokman Hekim University; conditions: Nursing Education; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 60; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] More than 300 million surgical procedures are performed worldwide each year. However, surgical errors remain among the most common medical errors causing preventable patient harm. Although various health policies have been implemented globally and nationally, adverse events continue to occur due to factors such as high patient volumes and insufficient staffing. One of the most important initiatives developed to prevent surgery-related adverse events is the World Health Organization's "Safe Surgery Saves Lives" project. Within this initiative, the Surgical Safety Checklist was developed and has contributed to significant reductions in adverse events. The World Health Organization has encouraged countries to adapt the checklist to their healthcare systems. In Türkiye, it was revised by adding an additional section based on the principle that "Safe surgery starts in the clinic." Current patient safety policies and initiatives largely focus on healthcare professionals. However, developing a culture of surgical safety should begin during undergraduate education. After graduation, students may adopt existing institutional practices regarding patient and surgical safety. Therefore, developing nursing students' knowledge, skills, and professional judgment regarding safe surgery before graduation is essential. This randomized controlled experimental study aims to compare the effectiveness of an artificial intelligence-assisted virtual simulation game and traditional simulation in improving nursing students' knowledge and skills regarding the Surgical Safety Checklist. The effects of these interventions on students' problem-solving skills and patient safety competencies will also be examined. Students, research fellows, and the statistician will be blinded. Data will be collected using the Surgical Safety Checklist Knowledge Test, Surgical Safety Checklist Skills Assessment Checklist, Problem Solving Inventory, and a scale assessing nursing students' patient safety competencies. Data will be analyzed using SPSS, with p\<0.05 considered statistically significant.

title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus
desc: Deep models often rely on spurious correlations that fail on underrepresented groups. Existing methods either correct human-specified bias attributes or infer unknown biases from the learned representation space. However, annotated attributes may differ from the shortcuts actually used by a model, while a single representation provides incomplete and potentially noisy evidence. Our key insight is that a bias obscured in one feature space may be clearer in another. In this work, we propose CHORD (Cross-view Harmonic Outlier Reversal for Debiasing), a multi-view framework that allows samples to "sing in chorus" across diverse representation spaces to achieve robust cross-view consensus. CHORD aggregates aggregates within-class partitions in each view, which is a proxy for specifying candidate biases, to debias the target representation and classifier without bias supervision. Experiments on seven benchmarks across vision, language, speech, and medical imaging show consistent improvements in worst-group accuracy. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/davelee-uestc/chord_debiasing_public .

title: Learning to Defer under Expert Drift
desc: The learning to defer (L2D) framework enables safety in machine learning and AI systems by allocating difficult or critical decisions to a human expert. However, most prior work on L2D assumes fixed expert reliability, overlooking temporal fluctuations in human performance due to factors such as fatigue and cognitive biases. Humans commonly exhibit such substantial, systematic performance shifts across a wide range of domains, from high-stakes settings such as radiology, aviation, and judicial decision-making, to everyday tasks such as crowdsourced image annotation. We propose Expert-Drift-Adapted Learning-to-Defer (EDA-L2D), a novel expert-aware L2D framework that explicitly models these temporal shifts by conditioning the deferral head on recent histories of expert outcomes via a sequence model. This history-aware approach enables adaptive deferral policies that anticipate reliability fluctuations and better allocate decisions between human and machine over time. We provide comprehensive experiments across three diverse tasks -- image classification, medical diagnosis, and hate speech detection -- including generalization analyses under realistic deferral conditions and irregular shifts in expert reliability. Our results show that EDA-L2D adapts more effectively than prior L2D methods to diverse temporal patterns of expert reliability, resulting in improved system performance and more effective deferral decisions. Code is available at https://github.com/ZiyaoMou/L2D-Expert-Drift.

title: A Blockchain-Enabled Federated Ensemble Framework for Privacy-Preserving Mortality Prediction Across Heterogeneous Healthcare Systems
desc: Objective: To test whether a smart contract that admits hospital-trained models to a shared mortality model only after peer hospitals verify their performance can exclude poisoned or substituted models, and at what cost. Design: Retrospective simulation study of a federated learning protocol. Methodology: In the Blockchain-Enabled Federated Ensemble (BFE), hospitals committed SHA-256 digests of locally trained XGBoost and random-forest models to a Solidity contract; peers posted digest-bound validation AUROCs, and the contract admitted models with a median peer AUROC of at least 0.70. Admitted models were pooled by weighted logit averaging (BFE-PW) or stacking (BFE-Stack) with federated recalibration. Code and drafts were produced with an AI coding assistant under the authors' supervision. Setting: Four hospitals simulated from one academic centre with age, renal case-mix and laboratory-availability skew; a data-scarce regime keeping 5-20% of each hospital's patients; and a natural partition by care era. Participants: 425,215 adult admissions (186,103 patients; 2.35% in-hospital mortality) in MIMIC-IV v3.1, with predictors from the first 24 hours. Interventions: BFE against centralised, local-only, FedAvg, FedProx, median and Multi-Krum FedAvg and federated logistic regression, under seven attacks on training, attestation, recalibration and model delivery. Main outcome measures: AUROC and AUPRC (joint patient-clustered bootstrap), calibration, attack effects, gas and transactions. Results: Under gross label flipping, FedAvg lost 29% of its AUPRC while the contract excluded the poisoned models in every seed (Multi-Krum FedAvg was equally protected); all substituted models were detected, and collusion blocked release. A targeted flip of female deaths passed the gate and lowered sensitivity for deaths in women from 32.8% to 27.5%; poisoned recalibration inverted BFE-PW (AUROC 0.098) unless a median-of-sites recalibration was used (0.902). With large hospitals, BFE-PW matched FedAvg in AUROC (0.902) and BFE-Stack matched FedProx (0.907 and 0.906), below local-only (0.910) and centralised XGBoost (0.915), with lower AUPRC; with 5% of the data, BFE-PW exceeded local models (0.866 against 0.844). Pooled calibration hid two-fold under-prediction at one hospital (observed-to-expected ratio 2.13), which a local intercept corrected (0.93). title: MicroBioAgent: an AI agent for automated microbiome analysis
desc: Microbiome data analysis demands customized workflows tailored to specific biological questions, sequencing modalities, and data properties. However, constructing and executing these workflows requires navigating heterogeneous software dependencies, reference databases, and multi-step parameter tuning. Here, we present MicroBioAgent, an autonomous, domain-specific agent framework that translates high-level biological queries into executable, study-specific pipelines across 16S rRNA amplicon, reference-based shotgun, and de novo assembly-based metagenomics. Rather than relying on static pipeline templates, MicroBioAgent employs a closed-loop execution architecture: it dynamically selects and runs bioinformatics tools within user-controlled environments while iteratively inspecting intermediate outputs to adapt downstream analytical decisions. Furthermore, to address the long-running nature of metagenomic computation, we introduce an asynchronous background task-management mechanism that reduces LLM token consumption by over 50% while enabling real-time plan adjustment and automated workflow resumption. We systematically evaluated MicroBioAgent across three benchmarks of increasing complexity: (1) paired amplicon and shotgun profiling of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes, (2) taxonomic and functional profiling coupled with machine-learning classification in a colorectal cancer cohort, and (3) de novo metagenomic assembly, metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) binning, and metabolic pathway reconstruction in a polyethylene degradation study. Across all benchmarks, MicroBioAgent faithfully recapitulated the primary biological findings of the original studies, exhibiting high analytical concordance despite expected tool- and database-dependent variations. In systematic robustness evaluations across 27 independent runs spanning three backbone large language models and three prompt-complexity tiers, MicroBioAgent achieved a 98.8% task completion rate and yielded highly reproducible diversity and differential-abundance estimates. MicroBioAgent establishes a scalable, adaptive paradigm for end-to-end computational microbiome research.
